follows: reports/c75 -- third of the four candidate-not-finding families with a decisive reject signature (94 rows, 77% exact-component mismatch)

the_shape.reading: 71% have the observation recording NOTHING on the slot while the engine emits an end-of-turn residual -- Leftovers, Spikes chip, poison

a_hypothesis_i_tested_and_only_partly_co.claim: the family name says boundary TRUNCATION, and 57% of rows carry |faint| with 60% carrying |switch|. The natural reading is that the observation window ends at a faint and the engine keeps applying residuals the protocol never records.
a_hypothesis_i_tested_and_only_partly_co.verdict: PARTLY REFUTED. A faint on the complaining slot explains 6 of 77, under 8%. The |faint| tags counted at family level are mostly on the OTHER slot. What actually dominates is a switch on the slot -- 40 of 77 -- and 31 rows have neither.
a_hypothesis_i_tested_and_only_partly_co.why_i_nearly_got_this_wrong: I counted |faint| across the whole protocol rather than on the slot being compared. The same partial-check error as C58 and C62: measuring a boundary-level property and attributing it to a slot. Caught by scoping the check to the complaining slot.

what_is_established: the engine emits end-of-turn residuals on a slot where the observation records none, in 71% of the family. A switch on that slot accompanies 52% of those. Neither a faint on the slot nor a switch explains the remaining 31 rows, so the truncation story is real for part of the family and unproven for the rest.
what_is_not: the mechanism for the 31 rows with neither a faint nor a switch, and whether the 40 switch rows are truncation or the per-Pokemon comparison problem C62 identified in a new guise. Both need the switch-safe comparison rather than a slot-level one.
status: PARTIALLY DIAGNOSED. Weaker than C76 and C77; recorded at the strength the evidence supports rather than rounded up to match them.
